note over IT, FKM ... end note is the ONLY content; sequencePlugin.parse refuses kind=incomplete ('Sequence diagram has no participants', src/diagrams/sequence/parser.ts:306, mirroring SequenceDiagram.java:591 participantsList.size()==0) because src/diagrams/sequence/command-note-factory.ts's noteCommand never registers the note's own referenced entities as participants. The block is a tab-indented title line ('\ttitle produces a green rectangle') followed by 'rectangle "C1" <<GreenContainer>><<RedContainer>> as C1'. descriptionPlugin.parse refuses (kind=syntax) because src/diagrams/description/parser.ts:336-337's dispatchCommand passes the RAW (untrimmed) lines array to matchAnnotationCommand (src/core/annotations/commands.ts:97, TITLE_RE = /^title.../ with no internal trim; upstream CommandTitle.java:56-66 matches against a pre-trimmed StringLocated line, so no equivalent gap exists there), so the leading tab defeats the anchor; class and state both PRE-TRIM each line before calling matchAnnotationCommand for exactly this reason (src/diagrams/state/parser.ts:147-149's doc comment: 'matchAnnotationCommand requires already-trimmed lines ... no internal trim'). description's own multiline-block rationale for keeping raw indentation (parser.ts:336) does not require the ANNOTATION-MATCHER call specifically to see untrimmed text. Fix: pass a trimmed copy of the line to matchAnnotationCommand in description's dispatchCommand, mirroring state/class. Verified: parseNameSection already handles the double-stereotype rectangle line correctly (isolated test); once the title line is recognised, the whole block parses clean and description wins (D3: lands in DESCRIPTION, matching the jar).

action action { action action1 action action2 } / process process { process process1 process process2 } -- classPlugin.parse ACCEPTS with zero refusal, producing an empty 'action'-then-'process' classifier pair with the nested lines silently dropped. Root cause: 'action'/'process' are NOT in class-command-containers.ts's rule 5b' descriptive-container-opener keyword alternation (line 89-90: rectangle|node|component|folder|frame|cloud|database|storage|artifact|file|card|queue|stack|hexagon|agent -- missing action/process, though CONTAINER_KEYWORD in class-descriptive-leaf-command.ts:50-51, which IS CommandPackageWithUSymbol's own SYMBOL alternation verbatim per that file's own doc comment, DOES include them), so 'action action {' falls through to the DESCRIPTIVE_LEAF_COMMANDS fallback (class-descriptive-leaf-command.ts:91-127) instead. That fallback's isContainerOpener exemption (line 112) lets it claim the line WITHOUT calling openNamespaceBlock, so the nested 'action action1'/'action action2' lines are never re-dispatched through the per-line loop and never reach the allowmixing gate. Standalone, 'action action1' alone IS correctly refused (verified in isolation) -- the gate itself works; only container-body nesting bypasses it. This is the SAME bug class class-command-containers.ts's own doc comment (line ~92-99) already fixed once for 'component C1 $tag1 {' (jebovo-64-rasa849, sodoza-93-nanu557), left open for keywords absent from rule 5b's list. Fix: add action/process to rule 5b's keyword alternation so the container opens for real and its body re-enters the per-line/allowmixing gate (D3: the nested 'action action1' line then refuses, the whole class attempt aborts, and description -- verified to accept these keywords generically -- wins, matching the jar). See class-command-containers.ts:89-90 and class-descriptive-leaf-command.ts:50-51,112 for the exact keyword-list gap and exemption, mirroring CommandPackageWithUSymbol.java:76-77's SYMBOL alternation and PSystemCommandFactory.java:169-175's getCandidate()==null SYNTAX_ERROR default this port's silent-drop never reaches.

database "DB 2" <<&file>> as Db2 (a QUOTED display, a <<...>> stereotype, THEN 'as alias') is accepted by src/diagrams/sequence/sequence-parse-helpers.ts:318 parseParticipantDeclaration, but no upstream CommandParticipant subclass matches that token order: CommandParticipantA3.java:51-64 is the only subclass with a STEREOTYPE slot at all, and its grammar is TYPE FULL(unquoted, [%pLN_.@]+) 'as' CODE STEREO? -- the stereotype sits AFTER 'as CODE', and FULL is never a quoted string. Verified against the real jar (scripts/oracle-render.sh): 'database Db2 <<plain>>' (unquoted, no alias) renders SEQUENCE; 'database "DB 2" <<plain>> as Db2' (quoted display + mid-position stereotype) renders DESCRIPTION for every stereotype form tried (plain text, icon glyph, sprite name) -- confirming the refusal is the token ORDERING, not stereotype content. This port's parseParticipantDeclaration is a single shared parser that does not enforce upstream's per-subclass token-order restriction. Fix: narrow parseParticipantDeclaration (or gate the stereotype capture) to refuse a <<...>> token positioned between a quoted display and 'as alias'. Sizing/exact regex split needs one more read of CommandParticipantA/A2/A4 before implementation -- flagged for the batch-2 executor, not resolved here.

'note left' (bare, no 'of', no participant token, trailing space only) followed by free text then 'end note'. src/diagrams/sequence/command-note-factory.ts's noteCommand pattern requires the literal 'left of'/'right of'/'over' plus a mandatory participant capture, so 'note left' with nothing after it matches NO command and refuses kind=syntax on the note body text two lines later. The jar renders this fixture as SEQUENCE (verified: golden SVG draws the note body text and an 'opt'/'ref' frame), so upstream accepts bare 'note left'. FactorySequenceNoteCommand.java:76-90's regex ALSO requires a PARTICIPANT token after POSITION (not optional), so the exact upstream path that accepts a participant-less 'note left' was not fully isolated in this pass -- ruled out: it is not an isIncomplete issue (jar renders full content) and not a note-position issue (both 'left'/'right' spellings exist upstream). Instrument next: bisect the real jar (scripts/oracle-render.sh) against a minimal 'note left' + 'end note' fixture with an explicit prior participant to find which command actually claims it before implementing.

B1 -() A1 / B2 -() A1 / B2 -() A2 -- classPlugin.parse ACCEPTS, auto-creating B1/B2/A1/A2 as ordinary classifiers plus 3 lollipop circles. src/diagrams/class/class-lollipop.ts:196-201's own doc comment documents the mechanism verbatim: 'The existing side must already be a declared classifier upstream (CommandLinkLollipop.java errors "No class X" and drops the whole line otherwise) ... this parser ... leniently auto-creates the existing side instead of silently dropping the line.' Since B1 (the ENT_THEN_LOL existing side of line 1) was never declared before this line, upstream's CommandLinkLollipop refuses 'No class B1', the whole class-diagram build aborts, and the source falls through to description, which independently accepts the identical 3 lines (verified: descriptionPlugin.parse on the same lines returns no refusal, auto-creating B1/A1/B2/A2 as 'interface' nodes with links) -- matching the jar's DESCRIPTION rendering (D3). Fix: give applyLollipop an existence check on the 'existing' side (distinct from ensure's create-or-find) and thread a refusal back through class-commands.ts's execute() the way class-descriptive-leaf-command.ts's state.executionRefusal already does. CommandLinkLollipop.java:186 and :206 both return CommandExecutionResult.error("No class " + quark.getName()) for an undeclared existing side; this port's applyLollipop (class-lollipop.ts:196-201) does not.

""" as pn #orchid } -- classPlugin.parse ACCEPTS, producing a single 'he' classifier with NO 'pn' child (verified in isolation: the outer line matches class-command-containers.ts rule 5b' fine -- 'rectangle' IS in its keyword list -- and opens a real namespace container via openNamespaceBlock, but the nested line's triple-quoted juxtaposed-string form ('..."""...' with no operator between adjacent quoted segments) does not match ANY class command's CODE/DISPLAY capture, including rule 9's DESCRIPTIVE_LEAF_COMMANDS -- so it is silently skipped by the per-line loop rather than refused with SYNTAX_ERROR the way upstream's getCandidate()==null would (PSystemCommandFactory.java:169-175)). D3: once class correctly refuses on the un-parseable nested line, the whole class attempt aborts and description -- confirmed to already have working nested-container-leaf grammar via parseNameSection's triple-quote handling in isolation -- wins, matching the jar.

The source is a single bare line: a URL (https://forum.plantuml.net/17007/how-we-can-disable-textlength-at-svg-generation), no other @startuml content. sequence refuses (no participant keyword, no arrow). classPlugin.parse ACCEPTS with zero refusal: verified in isolation it treats 'https' as an implicit class id and everything after the line's first ':' ('//forum.plantuml.net/17007/...') as a colon-shorthand member (BodierLikeClassOrObject.java:102-111's isMethod/addFieldOrMethod single-line member shorthand, ported at src/diagrams/class/class-member-parser.ts), auto-creating a bogus 'https' classifier with one member. jar routes this fixture to STATE instead, so upstream's own colon-shorthand member command (registered on ClassDiagramFactory too) must refuse a line whose 'class id' has no prior declaration and no other class-shaped content, deferring to StateDiagramFactory's bare-identifier state fallback (CommandState.java-family) the way state already claims the DESCRIPTION-title-whitespace cohort's rectangle lines once description also fails. Ruled out: not an allowmixing refusal (class produced a classifier, not an executionRefusal); not a sequence-side defect (sequence already refuses correctly). Pinning rather than fixing: narrowing class's colon-shorthand member command to refuse a bare, undeclared, URL-shaped id would need proving safe against every other single-line 'Name : member' fixture in the corpus (D9, narrow-never-widen) -- a corpus-wide pass, not a one-row special case.
